defect: PLAN §9's subtle pattern: 'control plan with no owner,' built as three monitored items spanning exactly the range prescore can and cannot see. M-1 (the primary CTQ) has owner_name='' -- a genuinely blank owner. M-3 has owner_name='the team' with owner_accepted=false -- a group name, not accepted. M-2 (the Improve change) has owner_name='TBD' with owner_accepted=TRUE -- a placeholder name marked as if a real person had accepted the role. Everything else on the plan (frequency reasons, OCAP coverage and elements, training verification, check-in schedule) is deliberately clean so the only signal is owner quality.

deterministic_layer.notes: Confirmed live: owner_named hard_flags on M-1 only (['M-1'], the genuinely blank owner); owner_accepted flags on M-3 only (['M-3'], named-but-not-accepted). M-2 ('TBD', accepted=true) never appears in either check's output -- plan_health.ownerless_item_ids and unaccepted_owner_item_ids both skip it entirely, because owner_named only tests '.strip()' truthiness and owner_accepted only tests the boolean flag; neither one reads what the name actually says. This is the fixture's central point: a placeholder name marked accepted is deterministically indistinguishable from a real one.

must_catch: M-2's owner_name is the placeholder 'TBD' (rubric R-CTL-03's own placeholder-name framing), not a real named person, despite owner_accepted=true -- this is the sharpest case: it passes BOTH prescore owner checks (owner_named only tests for blank; owner_accepted only tests the boolean flag) and is left entirely to judgment.
R-CTL-03 (control plan core) should verdict needs_work, and should name M-2's placeholder owner specifically -- not just restate the M-1/M-3 issues prescore already flagged.
schema_note: Nothing here is schema-blocked -- MonitoredItem.owner_name is schema-loose by design (control_plan.py's own docstring: 'an ownerless item must be SAVEABLE so the theater flag has something to render against'), and nothing ties owner_name's CONTENT to owner_accepted's truth value. 'TBD' + accepted=true is fully schema-legal, which is exactly what makes it the strongest form of this defect: it is indistinguishable from a real accepted owner to every deterministic check in this engine.
